page: Microsoft Azure E16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz. Based on the x86_64 architecture and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 275 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while graphics processing units are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute and memory capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25 percent at 2698.78 and the PassMark memory score reaching the top 25 percent at 2788.92. Uncached memory read bandwidth hits 80.83 GB/sec, and uncached write bandwidth registers at 45.68 GB/sec. Multi-core performance metrics align with mid-range averages, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10435.0, a PassMark CPU score of 21922.73, and Redis SET throughput reaching 16.14 million operations per second. In contrast, large language model inference on 7B models falls into the bottom 25 percent due to the lack of hardware accelerators and AVX-512 vector support.

The 8:1 memory ratio provides balanced cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads where allocating excessive compute cores merely to acquire RAM is inefficient. Although the temporary 275 GB SSD provides fast scratch space, persistent enterprise setups require managed network block storage. The instance fits in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and enterprise database management systems, big data processing, and enterprise memory-intensive applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocking at 3.525 GHz. It is provisioned with 128.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 275 GB local SSD for temporary storage. In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-quartile results in single-thread stress-ng compute and PassMark memory operations, complemented by steady mid-range multi-core scores and 16.14 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators, the system exhibits lower throughput on medium-sized LLM workloads. The configuration delivers cost-efficient resource density for workloads demanding substantial memory footprints without redundant compute scaling, making it well suited for in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data-intensive analytical processing.
